automation_evidence.quote: L refers to the pre-trained Large models that serve as the brain of the framework for anomaly detection.

metric_evidence.quote: policy H (enhance prompt by historical series) achieved the best performance in all metrics (it beats the two comparison methods as well).

evidence.quote: Due to the relatively small scope and short time for its data collection, ENLITEN serves as a case for the data-scarce scenario.

practical_problems.note: ENLITEN is used as a dedicated data-scarce case; the prompted pretrained LLM is compared with trained DSVDD, RETAD and FC-AE on it, but the amount of data is not varied. calibration: data amount not varied; single data-scarce case.
Human-readable explanations are claimed, but no faithfulness or reviewer study of the explanations is reported.

summary: SLEP lets a pretrained LLM detect power-system anomalies from prompted histories and reflections without training, matching or beating trained baselines on three electricity datasets including a data-scarce one; explanations are claimed but not evaluated.
